questions.question: Dr. Mamouni is the manager of an LLC with his colleague. One of them opposes a contract before it is concluded. According to Article 63 of Law 5-96, is this opposition enforceable against third parties?
options: Yes, if the opposition is notified in writing
No, the opposition has no effect on third parties
Yes, if the third party had knowledge of it
No, unless the manager is the majority partner
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'In the case of multiple managers, opposition by one manager to acts of another has no effect on third parties.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I must be careful in my negotiations.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, dies. His heirs do nothing for 60 days. Dr. Mamouni informs him of the consequences. According to the 2024 amendments, what is the possible sanction for inaction?
options: The company is automatically dissolved
The company continues without change
Dissolution of the company is the possible sanction
The shares are attributed to the surviving spouse
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'The proposed amendment does not expressly provide for the sanction of inaction by heirs within the 60-day period, but dissolution of the company is the possible consequence.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I must inform my heirs of this deadline.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, manager of an LLC, wishes to borrow from his company. Dr. Ibrahimi warns him of the prohibitions. According to Article 66 of Law 5-96, does this prohibition also apply to relatives?
options: No, only to the manager
Yes, it extends to spouses, parents, and in-laws up to the second degree
Yes, but only to children
No, relatives can borrow
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'The prohibition also applies to spouses, parents, and in-laws up to the second degree.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I must respect this rule.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, has a turnover of 750,000 DH. Dr. Mamouni asks him to check his tax regime. According to the GTC, which regime is he automatically subject to?
options: RNS
RNR
CPU
Flat-rate regime
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'RNR is the default regime for liberal professions whose annual turnover exceeds 500,000 DH.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'So I am under RNR.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, manager of an LLC, wishes to commit the company to a 5-year lease. A statutory clause requires him to obtain partners' agreement for any contract exceeding 2 years. Dr. Ibrahimi informs him of the risks. What happens if he signs anyway?
options: The contract is null and void
The manager incurs civil liability towards the partners
The company is automatically dissolved
The contract becomes the manager's personal contract
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'In the event of violation of a statutory limitation, the manager incurs civil liability towards the partners.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will obtain the partners' agreement before signing.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, a partner in an LLC, wishes to transfer his shares to a colleague. Dr. Mamouni reminds him of the rules. According to Law 5-96, is the transfer of shares between partners subject to approval?
options: Yes, always
No, transfer between partners is free
Yes, if the articles provide for it
No, unless the transfer exceeds 50% of the capital
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'Transfer of shares between partners is free, unless the articles provide otherwise.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will check our articles.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, as a natural person, has a turnover of 300,000 DH. Dr. Ibrahimi asks him to choose between RNS and RNR. According to the GTC, can he voluntarily opt for RNR?
options: No, RNS is imposed below 500,000 DH
Yes, opting for RNR is voluntary
Yes, but only with tax authority approval
No, RNR is mandatory above 500,000 DH
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'Any taxpayer may voluntarily opt for RNR, even if their turnover is below the regulatory thresholds.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will opt for RNR to better manage my expenses.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, manager of an LLC, wishes to have the company guarantee a personal loan. Dr. Mamouni warns him of the prohibitions. According to Article 66 of Law 5-96, is this permitted?
options: Yes, if the partners agree
No, this prohibition is absolute
Yes, for an amount under 50,000 DH
Yes, if the loan is for the practice
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'Article 66 prohibits managers from having the company guarantee or endorse their commitments to third parties.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will not make this request.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, wishes to amend the articles. Dr. Ibrahimi informs him about the procedure. According to Law 5-96, can the sole partner amend the articles alone?
options: No, a general meeting is required
Yes, he can amend the articles by personal decision
Yes, but only with approval of a statutory auditor
No, amending the articles is prohibited in a single-member LLC
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'The sole partner exercises the powers conferred on all partners. He can therefore amend the articles alone.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will proceed with the amendment.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, has a taxable profit of 180,000 DH. Dr. Mamouni helps him calculate his PIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of PIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'The progressive scale applies: 0-30,000 DH = 0%, 30,001-50,000 DH = 10% (2,000 DH), 50,001-60,000 DH = 20% (2,000 DH), 60,001-180,000 DH = 34% (40,800 DH). Total = 44,800 DH.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'It's important to calculate correctly.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni has an LLC with 2 partners. Dr. Ibrahimi asks him how ordinary decisions are taken. According to Law 5-96, what quorum is required for ordinary decisions?
options: Absolute majority of votes
Simple majority of votes
Three-quarters of votes
Unanimity
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'Ordinary decisions are taken by simple majority of votes of the partners.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will organize votes accordingly.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, manager of an LLC, wishes to buy a building. Dr. Mamouni asks him if this is possible. According to Law 5-96, does buying a building require partners' approval?
options: Yes, if the articles provide for it
No, the manager has all powers
Yes, it is a mandatory extraordinary decision
No, buying a building is prohibited in an LLC
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'The manager has the broadest powers. However, the articles may limit these powers by requiring prior approval of partners.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will check our articles.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, as a natural person, has a turnover of 500,000 DH. Dr. Ibrahimi asks him to choose between RNS and RNR. According to the GTC, what is the threshold that makes RNR mandatory?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'RNR becomes mandatory when turnover exceeds 500,000 DH. You are at the limit, you can choose.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will study both options.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, a partner in an LLC, wishes to withdraw. Dr. Mamouni informs him about the reimbursement of shares. According to Law 5-96, do shares have a patrimonial value?
options: No, they are worthless
Yes, they represent a patrimonial value
Yes, but only in the event of dissolution
No, shares are lost upon withdrawal
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'Shares represent a patrimonial value. In the event of withdrawal, they can be reimbursed or transferred.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will evaluate the value of my shares.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, manager of an LLC, wishes to hire his son. Dr. Ibrahimi informs him of the rules. According to the Labor Code, is hiring a relative subject to particular rules?
options: No, no particular rules
Yes, compliance with the Labor Code and absence of conflict of interest
Yes, prior court authorization
No, but a declaration to the Order is mandatory
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'Hiring a relative must comply with the Labor Code and avoid any conflict of interest, particularly regarding salary setting.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will respect these rules.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi has an LLC with a profit of 250,000 DH. Dr. Mamouni helps him calculate the CIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of CIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'For the 0-300,000 DH bracket, the rate is 10%. The CIT due is 250,000 × 10% = 25,000 DH.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'This is much more advantageous than PIT.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, as a natural person, has a turnover of 600,000 DH. Dr. Ibrahimi advises him to create an LLC. What is the main tax advantage of the LLC?
options: Total tax exemption
CIT rate of 10% on the 0-300,000 DH bracket
CM exemption
Deduction of all personal expenses
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'The LLC allows a CIT rate of 10% on the first 300,000 DH bracket, compared to a progressive PIT that can reach 37%.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will create an LLC.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, manager of an LLC, wishes to create a subsidiary. Dr. Mamouni asks him if this is possible. According to Law 5-96, can an LLC create subsidiaries?
options: No, it is prohibited
Yes, an LLC can create subsidiaries
Yes, but only with the agreement of all partners
No, only public limited companies can create subsidiaries
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'An LLC can create subsidiaries, subject to statutory provisions.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will study this possibility.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, the sole partner of a single-member LLC, wishes to increase the capital. Dr. Ibrahimi informs him about the procedure. According to Law 5-96, can the sole partner increase the capital alone?
options: No, a general meeting is required
Yes, he can increase the capital by personal decision
Yes, but only with approval of a statutory auditor
No, a capital increase is prohibited in a single-member LLC
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'The sole partner exercises the powers conferred on all partners. He can therefore increase the capital alone.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will proceed with the increase.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, has a turnover of 900,000 DH. Dr. Mamouni helps him calculate his CM. What is the amount of CM due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'CM for natural persons is 6% of turnover, i.e. 900,000 × 6% = 54,000 DH.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'This is a significant amount.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, manager of an LLC, wishes to distribute dividends. Dr. Ibrahimi reminds him of the rules. According to Law 5-96, is dividend distribution decided by the manager alone?
options: Yes, the manager decides alone
No, it is decided by the partners' meeting
Yes, but only for single-member LLCs
No, it is decided by the court
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'Dividend distribution is decided by the ordinary general meeting of partners.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will convene a meeting.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, as a natural person, has a tax deficit of 40,000 DH. Dr. Mamouni reminds him of the carry-forward rules. Under RNS, is the deficit carry-forward allowed?
options: Yes, against profits of the following 4 years
No, RNS does not allow deficit carry-forward
Yes, against profits of the following 2 years
Yes, only against the following year
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'Under RNS, the deficit can be carried forward against profits of the following 4 years.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will track this carry-forward.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, a partner in an LLC, wishes the company to buy back his shares. Dr. Ibrahimi informs him about the rules. According to Law 5-96, is a buyback of shares by the company possible?
options: No, it is prohibited
Yes, under certain conditions
Yes, but only with the agreement of all partners
No, only public limited companies can buy back their shares
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'A buyback of shares by the company is possible under certain conditions provided for by law and the articles.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will study the conditions.'

questions.question: Dr. Ibrahimi, manager of an LLC, wishes to take out an insurance contract for the company. Dr. Mamouni asks him if this is within his purview. According to Law 5-96, can the manager take out insurance contracts on behalf of the company?
options: No, partners' approval is required
Yes, it is an ordinary management act
Yes, but only for single-member LLCs
No, insurance contracts are reserved for the court
questions.explanation: Dr. Mamouni explains: 'Taking out an insurance contract is an ordinary management act within the manager's powers.' Dr. Ibrahimi: 'I will take out this contract.'

questions.question: Dr. Mamouni, after managing several legal aspects of his LLC with Dr. Ibrahimi, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Mamouni?
options: Become an expert in dental company law
Retire
Change specialty
Forget good practices
questions.explanation: Dr. Ibrahimi explains: 'Mastery of company law is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Mamouni: 'I will train in company law.'
